chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqteen, from his brother Al-Husayn, from Ali ibn Yaqteen, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the one who manages the charity of the tenth (khums/zakat) for one who is not problematic (i.e., trustworthy but perhaps not fully reliable in all matters), so he (peace be upon him) said: 'If he is reliable (thiqah), then instruct him to place it in its proper places, and if he is not reliable, then take it from him and place it in its proper places yourself.'

key_terms.ثِقَةً: Reliable/Trustworthy (a technical term in hadith sciences and jurisprudence)
key_terms.صَدَقَةَ الْعُشْرِ: Charity of the tenth (referring to khums or zakat on agricultural produce)
key_terms.مَوَاضِعِهَا: Its proper places (referring to the specific categories of recipients for the funds)

ai.seo_question: How does the Imam determine whether to trust a charity collector to distribute funds independently or to take them back?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle of 'taqlid' in financial administration, where the Imam delegates authority to a trustworthy ('thiqah') agent for autonomous distribution of 'ushr, while retaining direct oversight for those lacking full reliability. It reflects the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the integrity of the collector ('amil') as a prerequisite for valid disbursement, ensuring that charitable funds reach their rightful recipients without error or misappropriation. This mechanism underscores the balance between trust in qualified scholars and the necessity of accountability in religious finance.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Bin Yaqteen, from his brother Al Husayn, from Ali Bin Yaqteen who said,

‘I asked Abu Al-Hassanasws about the one who gives out the charity (Zakāt) of the tenth (10%) upon the one there is no problem with. So heasws said: ‘If he was reliable, so instruct him to place it in its (appropriate) place, and if he does not happen to be reliable, so seize it from him and place in its (appropriate) place’.
en.sarwar: 6. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hassan ibn Ali ibn Yaqtin from his brother Al-Husayn from Ali ibn Yaqtin who has said the following: “

I once asked abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about Zakat which is of the rate of one out of ten and one who distributes it among those who are not harmful. He (the Imam) said, ‘If he is trustworthy, instruct him to deliver it where it should be delivered; but if you cannot trust him, then take it from him and deliver where it should be delivered.’”
